WHAT HOLDS OWNERS BACK

What stands between a finished villa and its first legal booking.

LAND & ZONING01

The land may not allow the intended use

The title, zoning and spatial restrictions must support the villa’s intended use before it can operate legally.

Zoning rules explained →
BUILDING02

The approvals may not match the villa

PBG, approved building function and SLF need to correspond with what was actually built and how the property will be used.

PBG and SLF explained →
BUSINESS03

The operating setup may be incomplete

The correct business entity, NIB, KBLI and applicable tourism licensing must be in place for the intended accommodation activity.

NIB and KBLI explained →
COMPLIANCE04

The villa may still not be ready to operate

Registration, operational standards and other applicable requirements must be completed before accepting guests legally.

Operating requirements explained →

FAQ

Questions owners ask first

What types of properties do you work with?+

We work with villas, apartments and multi-unit properties. Each property is assessed individually based on its legal status and commercial potential. We only take on properties that we believe can be legally operated and positioned for the premium short‑term rental market. As a general rule, we focus on properties with the potential to generate at least US$500 per booked night.

Do I keep full ownership of the property?+

Yes. Your title or lease stays with you, and we take no stake in the property.

Which company operates the property, and how is it legal?+

One of 30+ licensed local management companies we partner with. Your property is operated under its licence. How operator licensing works.

What does the 25% cover?+

Day-to-day management, on-site staff and launch photography. The owner pays separately for licensing, OTA commissions, utilities, repairs and taxes.

How much does licensing cost, and how long does it take?+

It depends on the property. The audit sets out the scope, cost and timeline before you decide. What the legalization route involves.

What if my property can’t be licensed?+

Then we decline the project. You’ll know at the audit stage, before any money is spent. What the audit checks.

How and when am I paid?+

Monthly, in USD or EUR. Payment details are agreed individually.

Can I stay at the property myself?+

Yes, on dates that aren’t booked. It is run as an investment property, so guest bookings take priority.

Who is responsible for guest damage?+

Damage claims go through the booking platform’s resolution process. Specific arrangements are agreed for each property.

How long is the contract, and can I exit?+

The minimum term is one year. Within the first three months you can end the agreement, and the listing accounts are transferred to you.

What taxes apply, and who pays them?+

Rental income is subject to Indonesian taxes, which are paid from the owner’s share. We pay tax on our own management fee. Your exact obligations depend on how the property is held and are set out during the audit. Local tax registration.

Where can I read the current Bali rental regulations?+

In our Bali Property Legal Guide: zoning, PBG, SLF, NIB, KBLI, PT PMA rules and the 2026 changes, with links to the official sources.
